inputs.original_text: PARIS, France— In a case that has sent ripples of concern through religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France, a French abbot has been convicted under a controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” The conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), under France’s new law has ignited a [...]
inputs.modified_text: This is about more than one conviction. France’s new “psychological subjection” law gives authorities an elastic label they can use against communities they want to bring into line. Father Bernard Domini, the abbot leading the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, is being made an example of, while the public is being asked to see it as protection. That’s how control gets normalized: officials decide which beliefs are dangerous, then use vague language to make dissent look threatening. Today it’s this community; the precedent could be used against anyone inconvenient.
